analysis.title: CoTD: Apple, Oranges.... and Chips
key_insights: Jim Reid calls tonight's Nvidia earnings (11/17) probably the biggest event of the next few weeks, ahead of macro.
Nvidia net income was about $5bn a year when ChatGPT launched in Nov 2022. On a rolling four-quarter basis it is likely near $240bn now, and consensus has about $625bn by 2031.

If the 2031 consensus is reached, Nvidia's net income would exceed Saudi Aramco's roughly $160bn in 2022, the largest annual profit ever reported by the report's account, and would be about the size of the annual GDP of Thailand, the UAE or Austria.

Analysts' 2031 earnings forecast for Nvidia has risen from a little over $10bn (Nov 2022) to about $50bn (a year later), about $175bn (a year after that), roughly $280bn (a year ago) and about $625bn now.
Nvidia is down around 35% from its early-October all-time high and 16% over 12 months, while its 2031 earnings forecast has more than doubled over that period.

The report says the market is less sure hyperscalers can keep spending at this pace, and is asking whether competition and custom chips will squeeze margins and whether peak-cycle earnings forecasts for leading tech stocks are reliable.
At its current market cap Nvidia trades on about 6x the $625bn 2031 earnings forecast. At 16x those earnings it would be the first $10 trillion company.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reports earnings the evening of 11/17/2026. Rolling four-quarter net income is likely near $240bn (the report's estimate, not a reported figure). Consensus net income for 2031 is about $625bn (forecast).
risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex may not keep growing at the current pace.
Competition and custom chips could squeeze Nvidia's margins.
Earnings forecasts for leading tech stocks at their peak may not be a reliable guide.
